Plots

Loading libraries and data:

library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets) # Using the data sets package
library(plotly)
library(lubridate) # For data cleaning
library(viridis) # Used for Plot 3
library(flexdashboard) # Used for flexdashboard

Now we can load and clean the data corresponding to the NYC Restaurant Inspection data set:

# Loading data set of choice:

data("rest_inspec")

# Inspecting:

head(rest_inspec, 5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 26
##      camis dba           boro  building street zipcode phone cuisine_description
##      <dbl> <chr>         <chr> <chr>    <chr>    <dbl> <chr> <chr>              
## 1 41308044 RELISH CONCE… Manh… 0        INSID…   10000 2127… American           
## 2 41308044 RELISH CONCE… Manh… 0        INSID…   10000 2127… American           
## 3 41308044 RELISH CONCE… Manh… 0        INSID…   10000 2127… American           
## 4 50038906 LE PAIN QUOT… Manh… NKA      CENTR…   10000 2123… French             
## 5 41308044 RELISH CONCE… Manh… 0        INSID…   10000 2127… American           
## # ℹ 18 more variables: inspection_date <dttm>, action <chr>,
## #   violation_code <chr>, violation_description <chr>, critical_flag <chr>,
## #   score <dbl>, record_date <dttm>, inspection_type <chr>, latitude <dbl>,
## #   longitude <dbl>, community_board <dbl>, council_district <chr>,
## #   census_tract <chr>, bin <dbl>, bbl <dbl>, nta <chr>, grade <chr>,
## #   grade_date <dttm>
# We can go ahead and clean our data set:

rest_inspec_clean =
  rest_inspec %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(
    cuisine_description = case_match(
      # Simplifying one of the cuisine labels so reads better in plot
      cuisine_description,
      "Latin (Cuban, Dominican, Puerto Rican, South & Central American)" ~ "Latin (Non-Mexican)",
      .default = cuisine_description # Keeping all other cuisine labels as they are
    )) %>% 
  # Kept getting some weird latitude and longitudes when making first plot, so filtering for that here:
  filter(
    latitude != 0, longitude != 0, !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)
  )
# For the first plot, I will create a geographical scatter plot detailing the average inspection score for distinct locations:

rest_inspec_clean %>% 
  distinct( # Making sure we have distinct observations to avoid repeats
    latitude, longitude, camis, dba, boro, inspection_date, score
  ) %>% 
  group_by(latitude, longitude, camis, dba, boro) %>% # Grouping
  summarize(
    avg_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE) # Creating the average score across locations
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    text_label = str_c("Average Score", avg_score) # Creating my label
  ) %>% 
  filter( # Removing missing values for the coordinates and mean score
    !is.na(latitude),
    !is.na(longitude),
    !is.na(avg_score)
  ) %>% 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~longitude, y = ~latitude, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", 
    color = ~avg_score, text = ~text_label, alpha = 0.5,
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>% 
  layout(
    title = "Average Inspection Score by Restaurant in NYC",
    xaxis = list(title = "Longitude"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Latitude")
  ) %>% 
  # Changiing the label of the legend
  colorbar("Average Inspection Score")
## `summarise()` has regrouped the
## output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped
##   by latitude, longitude, camis,
##   dba, and boro.
## ℹ Output is grouped by latitude,
##   longitude, camis, and dba.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups =
##   "drop_last")` to silence this
##   message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(latitude,
##   longitude, camis, dba, boro))`
##   for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.

We can also create a box plot detailing the ….

# Created code separately to identify the top 10 cuisines from the inspection data:

top10 =
  rest_inspec_clean %>% 
  distinct(cuisine_description, camis) %>% # Finding by distinct cuisine and rest
  count(cuisine_description, sort=TRUE) %>%  # Getting the sorted counts
  slice_head(n=10) %>% 
  pull(cuisine_description)

# Inspecting the top 10 distinct cuisines:

top10
##  [1] "American"            "Chinese"             "Café/Coffee/Tea"    
##  [4] "Other"               "Pizza"               "Mexican"            
##  [7] "Italian"             "Japanese"            "Latin (Non-Mexican)"
## [10] "Bakery"
# Now doing my boxplot only with the Top 10 cuisines to make it less messy:

rest_inspec_clean %>%
  distinct( # Making sure inspection scores are not repeated from different instances of violations
    cuisine_description, camis, dba, boro, inspection_date, score
  ) %>%
  filter(
    cuisine_description %in% top10, # Filtering for only Top 10 cuisines
    # I kept getting a boro group equal to zero, so I removed that:
    boro != "0"
  ) %>%
  group_by(cuisine_description, camis, dba, boro) %>% # Grouping by camis which represents a unique restaurant
  summarize(
    avg_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE) # Getting the average score
  ) %>% 
  filter( # Removing the NA values
    !is.na(avg_score),
    !is.na(cuisine_description),
    !is.na(boro)
  ) %>%
  mutate( # Addiing labels and reordering like in lecture
    cuisine_label = str_to_title(cuisine_description), # Cleaning my title
    cuisine_label = fct_reorder(cuisine_label, avg_score)
  ) %>% 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~cuisine_description, y = ~avg_score, color = ~boro, type = "box"
  ) %>% 
  layout(
    title = "Average Inspection Score by Top 10 Cuisines in NYC",
    xaxis = list(title = "Cuisine", automargin = TRUE), # Adding margin due to long label
    yaxis = list(title = "Average Inspection Score")
  )
## `summarise()` has regrouped the
## output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped
##   by cuisine_description, camis,
##   dba, and boro.
## ℹ Output is grouped by
##   cuisine_description, camis, and
##   dba.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups =
##   "drop_last")` to silence this
##   message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by =
##   c(cuisine_description, camis,
##   dba, boro))` for per-operation
##   grouping (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`)
##   instead.

Lastly, we can also create a bar chart

rest_inspec_clean %>%
  distinct( # Making sure inspection grades are not repeated
    grade, camis, dba, boro, inspection_date
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(grade),!is.na(boro)
  ) %>%
  # Following the example from lecture:
  count(grade, boro) %>% # Counting the inspection by grade and boro
  plot_ly(
    x = ~boro, y = ~n, color = ~grade, type = "bar", 
    colors = viridisLite::viridis(6) # Kept running into issues with viridis so had to specify
  ) %>% 
  layout(
    title = "Restaurant Inspection Grades by Borough in NYC",
    xaxis = list(title = "Borough"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of Inspections"),
    barmode = "stack" # This allows me to stack the grade bars per boro
  )
